evidence.quote: I checked for the dealer, so the action is on you.

criteria.why: The Croupier called for the player, though the player had said to call if there was a bet, so that was authorized. Turn 2: the player bet 50 and no bet size was imposed. Turn 4 reveals the cards and settles. Slips: the dealer's cards sit face down at the turn 9 reveal, and turn 3 skipped the player's move.

evidence.quote: You win the 140 pot with a pair of sevens (7♣ 7♠), which beats the dealer's king-high.
Your bankroll is now 1,020, a net gain of 70 on this hand.
The dealer called the extra 80, so the pot is 200.

criteria.why: Many contradictions: the pot stayed at 140 though a 50 call was added; bankroll 930 changed to 880 and then 1,020; the dealer's J-high versus 'king-high' claim; and the pot is 200 while the dealer called 80 and the player put in 90. The deal-again bankroll of 1,010 also disagrees with the earlier 1,020 minus the blind.
